source.title: Grokking as Dimensional Phase Transition in Neural Networks

record.file_problem: The text includes garbled figure-label extraction, but the main text and captions are readable; it is not cut off.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures gradient-dynamics indicators during a grokking-like transition, using finite-size scaling and avalanche analysis rather than the original studies’ behavioral or circuit measurements.
record.gate_note: The study’s XOR experiment uses the same four patterns for training and evaluation, so it does not test delayed generalization on a held-out test set. Its claims about a Transformer on ModAdd-59 and shadow-probe controls are attributed to a companion study and are not counted as this study’s results.
record.test_reason: The study does not test any version. Its only experiment is XOR, where training and evaluation use the same four patterns and rise together at about epoch 27. There is no held-out test set, so no delayed generalization, and the authors call it an abrupt learning transition. The quantity it tracks is the finite-size-scaling dimensionality D of gradient avalanches under a diffusion probe. That is a gradient-geometry measure, not a generalizing circuit or the removal of memorizing components, so it does not bear on V2 either. The canonical ModAdd-59 and shadow-probe results belong to a companion study and are only cited here.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that grokking is a dimensional phase transition in gradient avalanche dynamics, with D crossing from below 1 to above 1, and that it shows self-organized criticality. They conclude D reflects gradient-field geometry rather than topology. They acknowledge XOR has no test split but call this a methodological feature. They claim, citing an unpublished companion study, that the same D(t) signature appears in canonical ModAdd-59 grokking and in ungrokked-run controls.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a threshold-based diffusion update and finite-size scaling of gradient avalanches on XOR MLPs; it does not reproduce the original algorithmic delayed-generalization experiment or identify the circuits studied in mechanistic interpretability work.
record.method_sensitivity: The synthetic-gradient D result is reported as topology-invariant across five topologies (CV < 0.3%) and robust across diffusion strengths α = 0.1–0.5 (CV ≲ 1%). The main model-scale analysis uses a Barabási–Albert graph.

fits_no_version.finding: In XOR MLPs, gradient-avalanche FSS dimensionality D rises from 0.90±0.02 before the transition to 1.20±0.02 after it. Synthetic Gaussian gradients give 0.99±0.01.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An abrupt learning transition on the training set coincides with a shift in gradient-avalanche dimensionality from below 1 to above 1.

fits_no_version.finding: The Gini coefficient of |θ| shows a transient +25% peak lasting about 50 epochs, aligned with the transition within ±10 epochs (1000 seeds).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight concentration peaks transiently at an abrupt learning transition.

fits_no_version.finding: Training and evaluation accuracy, measured on the same four XOR patterns, jump together at epoch 27. Transition epochs depend on model scale (12–134).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In XOR MLPs, the transition is abrupt training-set learning, not delayed generalization.

record.problems: The XOR experiment has no separate test split, so it does not directly establish delayed held-out generalization. The main model-scale experiment uses six independent seeds per scale; the ModAdd-59 and shadow-probe results mentioned are from a companion study, not this study.

untested.parts: No held-out test set, so no delayed test-accuracy jump. Dataset size is not varied.
No generalizing circuit is identified, no memorizing components are measured, and the measures are not tested for anticipating a held-out generalization jump.
No non-algorithmic data, initialization-scale sweep or weight-norm intervention.
No weight decay, no critical dataset size, no ungrokking.
No comparison of the algorithms learned across runs.
No optimizer or floating-point controls. SGD only.

missing.what: Aggregate FSS exponents across eight scales: D=1.00±0.02 and γ=1.15±0.06, with R²≥0.99.

record.verdict_notes: Single-author preprint. The key claims extending the result to canonical grokking rest on an unavailable companion study. The reader's V2 'supports' label is removed, because a gradient-geometry measure on a task without held-out data does not test circuit formation or anticipation of generalization.

versions.untested_parts: No separate test split is used in the study’s XOR experiment; the canonical ModAdd-59 result is attributed to a companion study.

The study measures gradient dimensionality and weight concentration, not formation of an identifiable generalizing circuit, removal of memorizing components, or whether a progress measure predicts a delayed held-out test-accuracy jump.
No non-algorithmic data, initialization-scale sweep, or weight-norm intervention is tested.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data is tested.
No weight-decay or low-norm efficiency account, critical dataset size, or ungrokking threshold is tested.
The study does not identify or compare algorithms learned across runs.
No adaptive-optimizer instability or floating-point softmax artifact is tested.

rows.subject: XOR MLPs, aggregate across eight hidden sizes
rows.operation_detail: Finite-size scaling of gradient avalanche dynamics over training
rows.value: D ≈ 0.90 pre-grokking, rises continuously through the grokking window, and reaches D ≈ 1.20 post-grokking
rows.uncertainty: not stated for the time-resolved values
rows.note: The text describes a 30% dynamic range and a continuous rise during the multi-scale grokking window.
rows.check: D(t) is a gradient-avalanche dimensionality measured during an abrupt fit of the training set, with no held-out generalization. It is not a measure of a generalizing circuit forming, so it does not bear on V2. Also, D is sampled only every 10 epochs while grokking epochs span 12–134, so the 'continuous rise' rests on coarse snapshots.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: XOR gradient-dynamics measurements across the tested model scales
reader_labels.reason: The measured progress indicators change across the transition: D rises continuously from about 0.90 to about 1.20, with distinct phase estimates, and weight concentration has a transient peak (r1–r4). These results support gradual change in the measured indicators, not the specific circuit account.
